message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and boots from Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
The example uses the **REST API** (via `curl`) and the **gcloud CLI** – pick whichever you prefer.

> **Important prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** and the **GPU API** must be enabled.  
> * You need a service account key (JSON) or an OAuth token with the scope  
>   `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.  
> * The GPU license for the RTX A6000 must be granted to your project.  
>   (See <https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus#license>)

---

## 1. REST API call (curl)

```bash
# Variables – change these to match your environment
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"

# Get an OAuth 2.0 access token (replace with your own method if needed)
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# Build the JSON body
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_BODY <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/$MACHINE_TYPE",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/$IMAGE_PROJECT/global/images/family/$IMAGE_FAMILY"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": $GPU_COUNT,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/$GPU_TYPE"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# Make the API request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$INSTANCE_BODY"
```

### What this does

| Section | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `machineType` | 8‑vCPU, 30 GB RAM instance. Adjust as needed. |
| `disks` | Boots from the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `guestAccelerators` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `metadata.startup-script` | Installs the NVIDIA driver automatically on boot. |
| `serviceAccounts` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access. |

---

## 2. gcloud CLI command

If you prefer the CLI, the same configuration can be expressed in a single command:

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=my-gcp-project \
  --zone=us-central1-a \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-standard \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535' \
  --scopes cloud-platform
```

> **Tip:**  
> * If you need more GPUs, increase `count=`.  
> * For a different machine type, replace `n1-standard-8` with something like `n1-highmem-16`.  
> * To use a persistent SSD for the boot disk, change `--boot-disk-type=pd-ssd`.

---

## 3. Verify the instance

After the API call or CLI command completes, you can check the instance status:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=us-central1-a
```

Look for the `status` field (`PROVISIONING`, `RUNNING`, etc.) and the `guestAccelerators` section to confirm the GPU is attached.

---

## 4. Optional: SSH into the instance

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=us-central1-a
```

Once logged in, verify the GPU:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

### Recap

* **REST API**: `POST /compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances` with a JSON body that includes `guestAccelerators`.  
* **gcloud CLI**: `gcloud compute instances create ... --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1`.  

Both approaches create an Ubuntu 20.04 LTS instance equipped with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU. Adjust the machine type, disk size, or other parameters to fit your workload. Happy computing!
